place: Salerno; then England, France, Germany, Italy
contents: about 137 complete copies + about 100 partial copies (roughly 240 in all)
note: Latin manuscript tradition, summary row. Ventura (RHT 10, 2015) counts 137 complete witnesses (12th-15th c.) and about 100 more with parts of the text; the Wellcome blog by Ventura gives about 240. Two main versions: versio A (enlarged, up to about 900 chapters: lost Breslau 'Codex Salernitanus' Stadtbibl. 1302, partly edited by Holler 1940; Tractatus de herbis, oldest London BL Egerton 747) and versio B / vulgate (250-280 chapters: Erlangen UB 674 edited by Wölfel 1939; Göttingen UB Hist. Nat. 12; the 'Lyon 1525' redaction = the printed text). Other key copies named in the literature: New York Botanical Garden MS 11 (Starkenstein A, late 12th c.); Wien ÖNB 2461; London BL Sloane 420; Basel UB K II 11 (illustrated); Munich BSB Clm 325; Wellcome MSS 536, 547, 624, 625. No critical edition yet; Ventura is preparing one.

Wellcome Library MS.624, the copy used by the project (pilot file 'École de Salerne Latin.pdf'). Paper, 71 ff., written in the 1440s-1450s (watermarks), no illustrations. Versio B, 'Göttingen' redaction (extra S-chapters De salice ... De sandalis on ff. 65v-66v); described by Ventura, RHT 10 (2015), p. 337 no. 53. Incipit 'Incipit liber magistri Johannis platearii'. Provenance Arnold Busson (1844-1892). Public Domain Mark; live work id m36jrrsj (b19625571).

contents: 1 early 13th-c. translation (1 copy known) + about 28 copies of the illustrated 'Livre des simples médecines'
note: Old/Middle French tradition, summary row. (1) A literal 13th-c. translation, Paris Bibl. Sainte-Geneviève MS 3113, edited by Dorveaux 1913. (2) The 'Livre des simples médecines', a late-14th-c. French adaptation of the Tractatus de herbis (versio A), 28 extant manuscripts per the Wellcome catalogue (a review cited elsewhere gives 23 complete copies); key copies: Paris BnF fr. 12322 (Malandin 1986), Brussels KBR IV 1024 (Opsomer 1980/1984), St Petersburg NLR Fr.F.v.VI.1 (Moleiro facsimile 2000), Modena Estense alpha.M.5.9 = Est. 28 and a second Estense codex (Camus 1886; Trident facsimile 2008), Wellcome MS 626 (c.1470). The printed Arbolayre/Grant herbier derives from this French tradition. Jonas (IRHT) work no. 2440 not consulted: site unavailable during this check.

work: Petit Bauhin, Histoire des plantes de l'Europe
note: Histoire des plantes d'Europe, ou élémens de botanique pratique. A Linnaean rewrite intended to replace the Petit Bauhin. The introduction names the Petit Bauhin, explains that its small woodcuts were reduced from Mattioli by Lyon booksellers around 1670, and reuses the woodcut blocks 'qui nous ont été confiées' (read via Internet Archive full-text search). New text, same pictures. IA b28777207_0001 and b28777207_0002 (Wellcome); IA bub_gb_6WJgCIP4vIQC (Google Books 6WJgCIP4vIQC).
